tasks.//build:pgo: The profile-guided pair the platform packages ship — the `release` CLI and the `napi`-profile addon, each trained AS ITSELF over the `../corpora` snapshot's `origin: own` collections (the CLI directly, the addon through the loader's `cli.js` and, for the type strip and the import records, in process; `parse` on every file, the strip on every TypeScript file, the import records on every TypeScript and Svelte file, then `format --jobs 1`), then rebuilt with the profile and LLVM's cost-benefit inliner off — staged into crates/tsv_napi/pkg/<host triple>/ where `build:napi:packages` stages the plain pair, so `test:napi:npm:run`, `engines:audit` and `validate:napi --pgo` grade it next. Every gate fails the run: the snapshot at its pinned tree with every own collection present (the manifest read from the pinned commit), the toolchain's own `llvm-profdata` (`rustup component add llvm-tools-preview`) in the instrumenting rustc's LLVM, a profile that counts function entries, in which every hot function was entered once per input of its class trained, `-Cprofile-use` on every workspace crate's compile and no profile diagnostic in the use builds but the build scripts', instrumentation sections in the trained binaries and none in the shipped ones, output byte-identical to the plain builds (format, parse, strip, import records), the `--pgo` size bands, and the depth limits' stack contract in the staged addon itself (scripts/pgo/addon_depth.ts; `--no-depth` skips it locally). The plain CLI, the instrumented pair and the profile-use pair are fat-LTO builds, and the depth shapes take a `corpus`-profile test build; the PGO builds go under `.pgo/` — outside `target/`, whose caches would serve an earlier profile's codegen. The release workflow runs the same steps one by one (scripts/pgo/pgo.ts module doc), uncached. Locally the task adds the bench's C-FFI library as a third world (`--ffi`, trained as itself, held byte-identical to its plain build) and passes `--reuse`: a stamp (.pgo/stamp.json, written only once every gate passed) keyed on a hash of everything that can change the binaries — every file of each crate the worlds compile (`cargo metadata`), the manifest, lockfile and toolchain pin, every cargo config cargo would read (this directory's parents' and cargo home's), the cargo/rustc environment (`CARGO_*`, `RUSTC*`, `RUSTFLAGS`, `RUSTDOC*`, minus output dir, job count, terminal and credentials), `rustc -vV`, `build.sh`, the repo modules the pipeline runs (`deno info` over pgo.ts, the training drivers — the bench FFI wrapper included — the staging and the size bands), the loader facade the addon trains through, the snapshot pin — skips the build and its gates when the key matches and the binaries are still the stamped bytes, restaging the pair and re-reading the size bands, and running the depth gate only when it has not passed for those inputs. `build:bench:pgo` runs the same pipeline into the same directory, so each reuses what the other built. The key leaves out the Node and Deno versions the drivers run under and the fixture trees `byteid` reads: neither changes a binary, but a fixture edit can expose a PGO/plain output difference a hit never re-grades — rebuild without `--reuse` to re-grade. `TSV_BUILD_FORCE=1` is the bench task's way to drop `--reuse`; here, run `pgo.ts all --ffi` without it.
tasks.//build:bench: Everything a bench leg measures or sizes: the profile-guided native pair every timed native row loads (`build:bench:pgo`), the two size-only FFI subset builds, which stay plain (no row executes them, and each would need a training of its own — a profile applies only to the feature set it was trained at), and the wasm bundles (never profile-guided).
tasks.build:bench: deno task build:bench:pgo && deno task build:bench:deno && deno task build:bench:node
tasks.build:bench:deno: deno task build:ffi:format && deno task build:ffi:parse && deno task build:wasm:deno && deno task build:wasm:parse:deno && deno task build:wasm:all:deno
tasks.//build:bench:pgo: The profile-guided C-FFI library (the Deno row) and N-API addon (the Node/Bun rows) the bench measures, staged in .pgo/bench/ beside a stamp naming their bytes, their profiles and their training (benches/js/lib/pgo_bench.ts) — what the freshness guard and the report's `native_build` read. Runs `scripts/pgo/pgo.ts all --ffi --no-depth --reuse` (scripts/pgo/bench.ts) in .pgo/, the directory and stamp `build:pgo` uses: a stamp-hit (the inputs hash as the stamped build's) skips the build and its gates in seconds, a miss reruns the pipeline — instrumented builds, training, profile-use builds, the build-log, section and byte-identity gates — in minutes. The depth gate is a ship gate, not a measurement one, so it is skipped. `TSV_BUILD_FORCE=1` drops `--reuse` (a change the key cannot see). Stages the pipeline's PGO pair into crates/tsv_napi/pkg/<triple>/ too, as `build:pgo` does — so a plain `validate:napi` over that staging afterwards fails its plain bands (`build:napi:packages` restages plain). Needs ../corpora at its pin and `llvm-tools-preview`.
tasks.//typecheck:js: Typechecks the JS/TS the repo owns that Deno runs — the bench harness and scripts/ — which `deno task typecheck` (cargo) does not see. Directory arguments, not per-directory globs: deno walks them (skipping node_modules) so a new subdirectory is covered the day it appears, where a glob list silently is not. NOT in `deno task check`: the harness imports npm packages by bare specifier, so this needs `deno task bench:install`, and CI's check job deliberately installs no bench node_modules (.github/workflows/check.yml). The node-modules-free halves are carved out into typecheck:scripts and typecheck:bench-core, which DO gate — so what only this task covers is the npm-importing part of benches/js (the impl wrappers, the corpus loader, the entry points) and scripts/doctor.ts. The tsv_debug sidecar runs on Node and is typechecked by `typecheck:scripts`' `tsc` program. Same posture as test:deno:canonical — run it after a harness or scripts change.
tasks.//typecheck:scripts: Typechecks scripts/ in two programs, each by the checker of the runtime its files run on, so it CAN gate in `check`: nothing else typechecks the release scripts, and `deno run` does not — so publish.ts / publish_napi.ts / build_napi_packages.ts, whose first real execution is a release, would otherwise reach it unchecked. First `tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json`, the scripts that run under Node: every root under `scripts/roots/` (a glob, so a new root is covered the day it appears) and what it imports, with Node's types and no `Deno` global, plus tsv_debug's sidecar (`crates/tsv_debug/sidecar/sidecar.ts`), whose packages resolve from its own install, so this half needs `npm ci --prefix crates/tsv_debug/sidecar` as well as the root's `npm ci`. Then `deno check` over the scripts Deno still runs, a DIRECTORY walk (a new script is covered the day it appears, where a file list silently is not) minus what the root config's `exclude` names: the Node scripts and their libraries, which import `@fuzdev/gro` and so cannot resolve here, and `scripts/doctor.ts` (see //exclude); the entries CI runs with no `node_modules` and on Windows (`build:stamped`'s, `build:napi:packages`' staging, `validate:napi`'s) and their libraries are in both halves, since they must import no package. That half is node-modules-free by construction, which is what lets it run on a checkout with no `node_modules`: every module it reaches resolves to relative paths and node: builtins. `--no-lock`: the repo is deliberately deno.lock-free. `DENO_NO_PACKAGE_JSON=1`: with the root package.json in view, Deno resolves a bare specifier through the node_modules npm installs from it, any package there, so a script's bare import would typecheck here and fail at its first real run.
tasks.typecheck:scripts: node node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json && DENO_NO_PACKAGE_JSON=1 deno check --no-lock scripts
tasks.//typecheck:bench-core: The bench modules where node-modules-freedom is INTENDED and which `typecheck:scripts` does not already reach — so the harness's loader/guard core and its report composer are typechecked by `deno task check`, not only by the ungated `typecheck:js`. Most of that core rides scripts/'s graph for free (`deno check` walks transitive imports, so test_npm.ts / test_napi.ts already cover check_artifact_freshness, source_mtime, napi, tsv_artifacts, runtime, types, reject_probe, locations_probe, and pgo/ffi_ops.ts covers ffi; loc_wire_client.ts covers tsv_debug_server, and `test:deno`'s divergence suite covers patterns and fixture_cases); the listed ones are what nothing else reaches, among them `loc_cross_grade` (its scripts/ importer, check_loc.ts, runs under Node, where `tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json` checks it with node_modules in reach) and the modules the `test:node` suites test (corpus_pins, diff_path, the divergence detectors' expected_errors and panic_errors, format_config_probe, loc_tolerance, parse_diff, parse_divergences, perf_omit, prettier_fixtures), which `tsc` typechecks there but with `node_modules` in reach. Note what the ROOT config buys, with `DENO_NO_PACKAGE_JSON=1` keeping the root package.json and the node_modules npm installs from it out of view: it declares neither `nodeModulesDir` nor `imports`, so this invocation cannot resolve a bare specifier AT ALL — the task therefore ENFORCES node-modules-freedom on these graphs rather than assuming it, and a future npm import under them fails loudly instead of quietly depending on a local install. ⚠ NOT the maximal checkable set, deliberately: ~25 benches/js modules currently check on a bare checkout, but most are the impl WRAPPERS (canonical, oxc, biome, tsc, swc, …), which qualify only because their npm imports happen to be dynamic — gating those would turn an ordinary dynamic→static refactor into a CI failure and impose an import style on modules whose whole job is loading npm. ⚠ A FILE LIST, with the same caveat as //test:deno: a new module belongs here only if it is deliberately node-modules-free AND unreached. To check a suspect, append a deliberate type error and see whether `deno task check` fails — that is the probe that found these.
tasks.typecheck:bench-core: DENO_NO_PACKAGE_JSON=1 deno check --no-lock benches/js/lib/wasm.ts benches/js/lib/harvest_stamp.ts benches/js/lib/loc_wire_client.ts benches/js/lib/fixture_documents.ts benches/js/lib/error_text.ts benches/js/compose_reports.ts benches/js/lib/corpus_pins.ts benches/js/lib/diff_path.ts benches/js/lib/divergence/expected_errors.ts benches/js/lib/divergence/panic_errors.ts benches/js/lib/format_config_probe.ts benches/js/lib/loc_tolerance.ts benches/js/lib/parse_diff.ts benches/js/lib/parse_divergences.ts benches/js/lib/perf_omit.ts benches/js/lib/prettier_fixtures.ts benches/js/lib/loc_cross_grade.ts
tasks.//build:check: The ONE `--profile corpus` build world every `deno task check` audit leg shares, built in ONE cargo invocation so the stack compiles once. The `tsv_debug` legs select `-p tsv_debug --features _internal_audits`; the two `tsv_cli` ones (`format:audit`, `discovery:audit`) need the `tsv` BINARY, which that selection builds only as a library dependency — and `-p tsv_cli` ALONE resolves features without `_internal_audits`, so it was a second, fully duplicated compile of `tsv_lang` → `tsv_ts`/`tsv_css`/`tsv_svelte`/`tsv_cli` in the same profile (20.5 s of the 30.4 s stack, on every edit; `ls target/corpus/.fingerprint | grep tsv_lang` showed the duplicate). Selecting BOTH packages in one invocation collapses them: `tsv_debug` depends on `tsv_cli`, so adding `tsv_cli` to the selection adds no feature the unified graph did not already carry, and a following `cargo run -p tsv_debug --features _internal_audits` is a 0.04 s no-op re-check rather than a rebuild. The legs therefore keep their own `cargo run` — freshness per leg, one world. ⚠ The `tsv` binary this builds carries the ledger / swallow seams COMPILED IN (inert until armed, so `format --check` is byte-identical), which is exactly why no perf task may measure it: `profile`, `bench` and the release artifacts build their own default-feature worlds and must keep doing so.
tasks.build:check: deno task build:stamped --profile corpus -p tsv_cli -p tsv_debug --features tsv_debug/_internal_audits --quiet
tasks.check: cargo fmt --check && deno task format:audit && deno task pins:audit && deno task docs:audit && deno task docs:audit:docsrs && deno task deps:audit && deno task package:audit && deno task typecheck && deno task typecheck:features && deno task typecheck:scripts && deno task typecheck:bench-core && deno task conformance:audit && deno task conformance:audit:compiler && deno task variants:audit && deno task scan:audit && deno task fanout:audit && deno task roundtrip:audit && deno task roundtrip:audit:prettier && deno task discovery:audit && deno task canonicalize:audit && deno task binding:audit && deno task authoring:audit && deno task paren:audit && deno task razor:audit && deno task fuzz:audit && deno task fuzz:audit:debug && deno task test:node && deno task test:deno && deno task test && deno task test:depth && deno task test:audits && deno task swallow:audit && deno task comments:audit && deno task gaps:audit && deno task blanks:audit && deno task fabrication:audit && deno task census:audit && deno task width:audit && deno task ignore:audit && deno task check:ast-types && deno task check:loc && deno task lint
tasks.//check:loc: The `loc` CROSS-GRADE: tsv's two implementations of one `loc` definition — the Rust writers' loc wire and the shipped `crates/tsv_wasm/npm/locations.js` reconstruction of the span-only wire — deep-equal (key order ignored) over every parseable fixture document — each input and its format variants, which need no oracle (a prettier-side form tsv rejects is counted, not failed; `loc_wires`' module doc). The fixtures pin the span-only wire, so this is the only `check` leg that grades `loc`; its outside reference (acorn / Svelte) is `corpus:compare:parse`'s loc arm, at conformance cadence. One `tsv_debug loc_wires` process streams both wires as NDJSON, so it needs no sidecar and no node_modules. See docs/audits.md §Loc Cross-Grade.
tasks.//strip:corpus: The type strip's CORPUS differential (benches/js/strip_corpus.ts): tsv_ts::strip against ts-blank-space over the strippable TypeScript of the `gates` view's snapshot tiers, failing on a panic, a contract or idempotence finding, an output that is no JS module, a byte or refusal disagreement outside its reviewed ACCEPTED list, a stale entry, or a count off STRIP_CORPUS_PINS. Reads ../corpora and node_modules, so it is NOT in `check`; a `conformance` leg. tsv's side is one `target/corpus/tsv_debug strip --stdin` process, hence `build:check`; `:run` skips the build (freshness-guarded).
tasks.strip:corpus: deno task build:check && deno task strip:corpus:run
tasks.//imports:corpus: The import records' CORPUS differential (benches/js/imports_corpus.ts): tsv_ts::parse_imports / tsv_svelte::parse_imports against oxc-parser's module record over the JS/TS-family files and Svelte components of the `gates` view's snapshot tiers (a component's scripts found by svelte/compiler), every structural difference between the two models a named normalization, failing on a panic, a parse error on either side, a record or hasModuleSyntax difference outside its reviewed ACCEPTED list, a stale entry, or a count off IMPORTS_CORPUS_PINS. Reads ../corpora and node_modules, so it is NOT in `check`; a `conformance` leg. tsv's side is one `target/corpus/tsv_debug imports --stdin` process, hence `build:check`; `:run` skips the build (freshness-guarded).
tasks.imports:corpus: deno task build:check && deno task imports:corpus:run
tasks.fuzz:audit: cargo run --profile corpus -p tsv_debug --features _internal_audits --quiet fuzz --seed 0 --iterations 5000 && deno task fuzz:audit:css && deno task fuzz:audit:ts
tasks.//perf:ab: Parse / format performance A/B between two trees per language (TS, Svelte, CSS), plus the type strip: wall-clock medians plus `instructions:u` from `perf stat`, exit 1 when a row regresses. Builds each side from a git snapshot of its build inputs in `~/.cache/tsv/perf_ab/` (keyed by a hash of the build inputs' `git ls-tree -r -z` entries minus the overlaid drivers, so a tests- or docs-only change reuses the binary, and each binary by its driver's content and the build recipe, so a recipe change rebuilds; the most recently used few kept) with the current `crates/tsv_debug/examples/perf_ab.rs` and `perf_ab_strip.rs` drivers overlaid (a tree without the type strip builds only the first, and the run skips the strip rows loudly), in a cleared environment — the `--allow-env` list is exactly what a build keeps (toolchain lookup + `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS`), so a caller's `RUSTFLAGS` / `CARGO_PROFILE_*` cannot reach one side's build. The candidate defaults to the working tree. Broad `--allow-run`: the driver binaries live at cache paths no allow-list can name ahead of time; `--allow-write` bounds the script's own writes only (child processes are not held to it — the working-tree snapshot writes loose objects into the repo's object store). NOT in `check` — it builds two release trees. Rule + rationale: docs/performance.md §Gating a change against a base.
tasks.//branch:report: One document comparing two refs on every axis a merge read needs (sizes, type widths, work counters, recursion depth; build wall and timing behind --timing; see scripts/branch_report/branch_report.ts). Builds each ref from git in its own tree and target dir under ~/.cache/tsv/branch_report, and writes report.md + report.json. The same ref on both sides is the A/A null, whose JSON is the floor for later timing rows (--aa). A missing tool, skip or failed build is reported and exits non-zero unless --accept-gaps. NOT in `check` — it builds two release trees.
tasks.//bench: The full refresh, and the one caller that composes TWICE — deliberately. `bench:perf` ends with `bench:compose` so it stands alone, but compose reads `report.conformance.node.json` for the combined report's `conformance_vintage`, and `bench:conformance` rewrites that file AFTER it. Without the trailing compose the combined report a full run publishes describes the PREVIOUS conformance run — stamping `stale: true` and an older commit at the exact moment both halves were just refreshed at the same one, and naming the wrong half in the remedy. The re-run reads four JSON files and writes two; the alternative (moving compose out of `bench:perf`, or chaining it onto `bench:conformance`) breaks a perf-only or conformance-only machine.
tasks.bench: deno task bench:perf && deno task bench:conformance && deno task bench:compose
tasks.//bench:perf: Builds the whole artifact set ONCE, then measures it under each runtime with the `:run` legs (freshness-guarded, so the order is provable rather than assumed). Chains `bench:harvest:svelte-styles` and NOT the suite harvests: the corpus VIEWS decide who needs which cache, and the perf view holds only the `benched` svelte_styles cache (benches/js/CLAUDE.md §Harvests).
tasks.bench:perf: deno task bench:runtimes && deno task bench:harvest:svelte-styles && deno task build:bench && deno task bench:deno:run && deno task bench:node:run && deno task bench:bun:run && deno task bench:compose
tasks.//bench:deno: Every standalone per-runtime leg (`bench:deno` / `bench:node` / `bench:bun`, and `bench:conformance`) builds the WHOLE artifact set, not its own half. Each leg REPORTS the same tsv binary-size rows, cross-binding by design: `binary_sizes.ts` sizes the tsv artifacts by PATH rather than by the impl registry, so the deno report carries `tsv (napi)` and the node/bun reports the `tsv (ffi)` trio. Built per half, a leg would size the other half at whatever commit it was last built while sizing its own at HEAD, inside sibling reports all stamped with one `git_commit`. `lib/check_artifact_freshness.ts` warns when a `:run` leg is about to do exactly that (`warn_stale_reported_artifacts`); building everything is what makes the warning unreachable here. Warm, the other half costs about a second (`run_if_stale` skips each wasm-pack, cargo no-ops, `build:bench:pgo` skips on a current stamp).
tasks.bench:deno: deno task build:bench && deno task bench:deno:run
tasks.//rsvelte-allow-run: The rsvelte-fmt row spawns a prebuilt binary (it ships no in-process API — see benches/js/lib/rsvelte.ts), so `smoke` must permit it by path (a bench run's pre-flight child is granted the one installed binary by `benches/js/lib/bench_child.ts`). All five published platform packages are listed because the task string is static while the installed one is per-machine; Deno ignores a nonexistent path entry silently (unlike a bare NAME, which logs a resolution failure), so the four that don't apply cost nothing. Node and Bun need no equivalent.
tasks.//bench:deno:run: The ORCHESTRATOR's permissions only. A bench run is several processes (benches/js/bench.ts §Process model): this one loads no engine and no corpus — it starts the pre-flight process and one process per timed row per pass, and writes the report — so it asks for read, write to the results directory, and to run `deno` (its children) and `git` (the report's commit). What the children may do (FFI, the rsvelte-fmt binary, gzip, net) is stated once, in benches/js/lib/bench_child.ts, since Deno hands a child none of its parent's permissions. `--v8-flags=--expose-gc` is passed on to the children, which is where it is used.
tasks.bench:node: deno task build:bench && deno task bench:node:run
tasks.bench:bun: deno task build:bench && deno task bench:bun:run
tasks.bench:conformance: deno task bench:pins:suites && deno task build:bench && deno task bench:conformance:run
tasks.//bench:harvest: Two groups, split because their consumers differ (benches/js/CLAUDE.md §Harvests is the full argument). `bench:pins:suites` is the conformance-view group: the five SUITE caches (wpt / test262 / ts-repo / svelte-rejects / prettier-jsx) plus the CSS reject PIN, which harvests nothing but is stamped and graded the same way — all `--if-present`, so each warn-skips an input it cannot see, which is what lets the group preflight `conformance` on a partial machine. WHAT it cannot see is the corpus loader's call, not each leg's: the two reject pins and the prettier-jsx harvest load through `load_pinned_language_corpus`, whose `{ complete_for: <language> }` policy refuses an absent entry that could hold that language (`optional` ones INCLUDED — `optional` says only that an ordinary run may proceed without it, never that a pinned count still describes the corpus) and waves through one that cannot. Spelling that tolerance as a plain allow-missing instead is the bug the policy exists to prevent (benches/js/CLAUDE.md §Harvests). `bench:harvest:svelte-styles` is the perf-view group of one: stamped on the ../corpora `collections/` tree id + its EXACT block pin + the perf view's entry list (skips instantly when none moved), and it FAILS rather than warn-skips on a missing snapshot collection. This task stays the manual refresh-everything entry point.
tasks.bench:harvest: deno task bench:pins:suites && deno task bench:harvest:svelte-styles
tasks.bench:pins:suites: deno task bench:harvest:wpt && deno task bench:harvest:test262 && deno task bench:harvest:ts-repo && deno task bench:harvest:svelte-rejects && deno task bench:harvest:prettier-jsx && deno task css:over-acceptance:pin
tasks.corpus:compare:format: deno task build:ffi:corpus && deno task corpus:compare:format:run
tasks.corpus:compare:parse: deno task build:ffi:corpus && deno task build:check && deno task corpus:compare:parse:run
tasks.//wire:audit: The WIRE-INJECTION audit: the parse-side sibling of gaps/blanks — those inject into a fixture and grade the FORMATTER, this injects whitespace into every Svelte tag/block head and grades the resulting WIRE against the canonical parser (benches/js/lib/wire_inject.ts). Runs as a CENSUS (`--inject-limit 0`, every site), since a sample cannot be ratcheted. Green, but not in `check`: it needs the canonical parser, so conformance-tier. `wire:audit:terminators` is the lone CR / U+2028 / U+2029 family — document-wide, so a strided SAMPLE that cannot be ratcheted either, and ⚠️ RED BY DESIGN, like compile:fuzz. Model, coverage, blind spots: docs/audits.md §Wire-Injection Audit.
tasks.conformance:svelte-fixtures: deno task build:ffi:corpus && deno task conformance:svelte-fixtures:run
tasks.conformance:ts-fixtures: deno task build:ffi:corpus && deno task conformance:ts-fixtures:run
tasks.conformance:ts-repo: deno task build:ffi:corpus && deno task conformance:ts-repo:run
tasks.css:over-acceptance: deno task build:ffi:corpus && deno task build:wasm:all:deno && deno task css:over-acceptance:run
tasks.//css:over-acceptance:pin: The PIN alone — oracle only, no FFI/WASM build, freshness-stamped like the suite harvests, `--if-present` like them — so `bench:pins:suites` can carry `CSS_REJECTS_PIN` on the same cadence as its siblings instead of leaving it to a hand run (the one pin that once had no cadence at all). `--force` re-grades past a fresh stamp.
tasks.ts-repo:over-acceptance: deno task build:ffi:corpus && deno task build:wasm:all:deno && deno task ts-repo:over-acceptance:run
tasks.//conformance: The sidecar-cadence aggregate. `fixtures:validate` and `compile:fixtures:validate` preflight it as the ORACLE-FRESHNESS legs: `deno task check` runs each fixture tree's sidecar-free slice via cargo test, which grades tsv against the COMMITTED `output_prettier.*` / `expected_server.js` and so stays green when tsv and the committed file drift away from the live oracle together. Only a run that re-formats through prettier itself can see that — 17 s for all 4307 parser/formatter fixtures, which is why it gates here rather than living in a command someone has to remember. It cannot gate in `check`: that job runs on a bare CI checkout with no npm install, and the sidecar resolves its oracles from npm. `bench:pins:suites` preflights ahead of them as the PIN-FRESHNESS leg: the conformance-view count pins it re-derives are graded by no other cadence (docs/gate_counts.md §Where the numbers live), and it is ordered after `pins:audit:checkouts` (which names the checkout that moved) and before the fixture legs, so a corpus move is reported before anything expensive runs — seconds when nothing moved, and each leg warn-skips an absent checkout so a partial machine still reaches the legs below. `bench:harvest:svelte-styles` runs later, beside the corpus legs that read its cache: it loads the PERF view, where every ../corpora snapshot collection is REQUIRED, so it fails rather than warn-skips — the same requirement `corpus:compare` imposes a step later (benches/js/CLAUDE.md §Harvests). `strip:corpus:run` follows `build:check`, whose `tsv_debug` it drives: the type strip's differential against ts-blank-space, its own process since it asks nothing of the FFI or the canonical oracles (seconds); `imports:corpus:run` follows it on the same footing, the import records' differential against oxc-parser's module record.
tasks.conformance: deno task pins:audit:checkouts && deno task bench:pins:suites && deno task fixtures:validate && deno task compile:fixtures:validate && deno task bench:harvest:svelte-styles && deno task build:ffi:corpus && deno task build:check && deno task strip:corpus:run && deno task imports:corpus:run && TSV_FFI_PROFILE=corpus PRETTIER_DEBUG=1 deno run --allow-ffi --allow-read --allow-env --allow-net --allow-sys --allow-run=cargo,target/corpus/tsv_debug --allow-write=benches/js/.cache benches/js/conformance.ts
tasks.conformance:all: deno task conformance:test262 && deno task conformance
tasks.//test:deno: The suites still on `deno test`, the ones whose module under test calls `Deno.*` in the paths they test, so they gate in `deno task check` beside `test:node` (vitest under Node, which runs the rest; docs/tasks.md §`test:node`): `benches/js/lib/divergence/fixture_coverage_test.ts`, every divergence detector against its own committed fixtures, read through `fixture_cases.ts`'s Deno file reads (`--allow-read`); `scripts/perf_ab_test.ts`, perf:ab's tree listing and its strip entry-point probe against a scratch git repo, with `scripts/branch_report/side_test.ts`, the branch report's corpus identity over one — the tests that spawn a process and write, so they run as a second invocation with `--allow-write --allow-run=git`, plus `--allow-env` for exactly the three variables that point git at another repo (`GIT_DIR`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`), which perf_ab_test.ts clears so a run under a git hook cannot write the outer repo's index. Named paths, so a new Deno suite has to be added by name. Each invocation runs with `DENO_NO_PACKAGE_JSON=1`, so the root package.json and the node_modules npm installs from it stay out of their resolution, as in `typecheck:scripts`, and a bare import still fails them; and with `--no-config`, because the root config's `exclude` drops every `scripts/**/*_test.ts` from Deno's walks (see //exclude) and would drop these named ones too.
tasks.test:deno: DENO_NO_PACKAGE_JSON=1 deno test --no-config --allow-read benches/js/lib/divergence/fixture_coverage_test.ts && DENO_NO_PACKAGE_JSON=1 deno test --no-config --allow-read --allow-write --allow-run=git --allow-env=GIT_DIR,GIT_INDEX_FILE,GIT_WORK_TREE scripts/perf_ab_test.ts scripts/branch_report/side_test.ts
tasks.test:npm: deno task build:npm:format && deno task test:npm:run
tasks.//test:npm:run: The three wasm package suites' `:run` tasks have a SECOND spelling: scripts/publish.ts Step 6 runs `node --test scripts/test_npm.ts` per package itself (its own `PKG_DIR` loop, then `test:bun` once over all three with `--require-bun`) rather than calling these tasks. A leg added to one of them here is therefore NOT run by a publish until publish.ts gains it too — change both together.
tasks.test:npm:run: PKG_DIR=crates/tsv_wasm/pkg/format/npm node --test scripts/test_npm.ts && deno task test:bun format
tasks.test:npm:parse: deno task build:npm:parse && deno task test:npm:parse:run
tasks.test:npm:parse:run: PKG_DIR=crates/tsv_wasm/pkg/parse/npm node --test scripts/test_npm.ts && deno task test:bun parse
tasks.test:npm:all: deno task build:npm:all && deno task test:npm:all:run
tasks.test:npm:all:run: PKG_DIR=crates/tsv_wasm/pkg/all/npm node --test scripts/test_npm.ts && deno task test:bun all
tasks.test:napi: deno task build:napi:probe && deno task test:napi:run
tasks.test:napi:npm: deno task build:napi:packages && deno task test:napi:npm:run
tasks.test:napi:npm:run: node --test scripts/test_napi_npm.ts && deno task test:bun napi
tasks.//release:notes: The GitHub Release body for a tag: CHANGELOG.md's stamped `## <version>` section, printed. What release.yml's `release` job feeds to `gh release create`; run locally to preview what a tag would say. Fails on a missing or empty section — at a release tag it exists by construction (publish.ts refuses to stamp an empty `## Unreleased`).
tasks.//release:assets: The GitHub Release assets for a PUBLISHED version — every platform package's native `tsv` CLI binary + SHA512SUMS — pulled back from the npm registry (not the build artifacts), so the asset is byte-identical to what npm serves, re-run or not — plus the third-party NOTICE, copied from the checkout. `--out <dir>` (no `--` separator). Run locally against any released version to re-derive a release's SHA512SUMS from npm. The registry reads retry for a bounded window (the constants at the top of the script — the workflow runs this seconds after the publish, and a just-published version can lag the registry's read path), so a typo'd version fails after that window, not before.

//exclude: `scripts/doctor.ts` is here for the ROOT config only — it is the one scripts/ module that reaches the bench node_modules (its corpus probe imports benches/js/lib/corpus.ts), so a root-config walk cannot check it on a clean checkout. typecheck:js walks scripts/ under benches/js/deno.json, which has no exclude, so doctor.ts is still typechecked there. See the //typecheck:scripts note. `scripts/**/*_test.ts` is out of the root config's walks because most of those suites run under vitest and import it, which `typecheck:scripts` cannot resolve: `tsc -p tsconfig.vitest.json` (in `test:node`) typechecks the vitest suites, and `deno test` typechecks the ones still its own, which `test:deno` names under `--no-config`. The rest are the scripts that run under Node over `@fuzdev/gro`'s host modules, which this walk cannot resolve: `scripts/roots` (a new root is out of the walk the day it appears) and, by name, each library a root imports that imports `@fuzdev/gro` itself, even as a type, so a new such library joins this list or the walk fails on its import. `tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json`, `typecheck:scripts`' other half, checks them all (see //typecheck:scripts). The `!scripts/roots/…` names put back in the walk the entries CI runs with no `node_modules` and on Windows (`build:stamped`'s, `build:napi:packages`' staging, `validate:napi`'s): each and its library import no package (docs/tasks.md §`build:stamped`, §`build:napi:packages`, §`validate:napi`), and this walk, which resolves no package, is what holds them to it.
